## TL;DR

The desktop Work board search now sits in the page header row, left of the Human and Held toggles, at half its old width (420px to 210px). The "Search: <text>" chip is gone. Clear filters still clears the search and still appears while a search is active. The Client board link is hidden on the Work page behind a named flag; the `/client-board` route and page are untouched. The phone queue is unchanged because it never had the chip bar.

## Work and rationale

- `BoardQueueSearch.vue`: the root width changed from `min(100%, 420px)` to `min(100%, 210px)`. Behaviour is unchanged: it writes `q` to the URL, keeps a local draft, and shows the clear button only when there is text.
- `WorkView.vue`: the search moved into `.work-header-actions` in the slot the Client board link held, rendered only in the board view. The standalone search row below the header is removed. The link is wrapped in `v-if="showClientBoardLink"` with that constant set to `false`, so restoring it is a one-line change.
- `lib/workQueueFilters.ts`: `workQueueFilterChips` no longer emits a `q` chip. `hasActiveWorkQueueFilters` still counts the query, so the chip bar and Clear filters still show when only a search is set, and Clear still removes `q` through `clearWorkQueueFilterQuery`.
- `user-docs/concepts.md`: the Client board section said to open it from the Work Queue. It now says the Work Queue does not link to it and gives the address.

I kept the change in the header component and the chip helper, not in a new component. The search was already its own component, and the layout change is a question of where the parent places it.

## Approaches tried

I first considered hiding the whole chip bar when only a search is set. That would have broken Clear filters, which the task requires to keep working, so I kept the bar and let it show Clear filters alone. This leaves a bar with no chips when only a search is active. I think that is acceptable, but it is a visible consequence worth a reviewer's eye.

I considered making the search flex to fill the remaining header width. I used a fixed 210px maximum instead, because the spec asked for about half the current width, and fixed width keeps the toggles from shifting as the title changes.

## Challenges and blockers

- The existing tests asserted the `q` chip and the Client board href in several places. I updated them: the chip assertions, the header order test, and the stories-inbox assertion, which now expects no `a.client-board-link`.
- The WebKit chip-bar fixtures count chips. The long set now expects four, the short set one, and I added a search-only case that expects zero chips with Clear visible.
- I added a WebKit fixture that renders the real `.work-header` markup from a mounted WorkView at 720, 768, 900 and 1000px. It checks for document overflow and for pairwise overlap among the header children, and asserts the search is at most 210px and no Client board link is present. The screenshots I looked at at 720 and 1000px show the search at half width beside the toggles, with the view switch and New task wrapping to a second line at 720px. The sort dropdown renders as a plain list in those screenshots because the test's `Select` stub renders its items. That is a fixture artifact, not a UI bug.
- The vitest run over the five affected files passes: 95 tests, including the WebKit fixtures, after `bun run build:ui`.

## Key learnings

- A flag constant in the template is a clean way to hide a link without deleting its route. It also keeps the restore path obvious to the next person.
- Chip helpers are read by more than one test file. Changing the helper's output needs the tests that count chips, the Clear control, and pipeline behaviour all updated together. Grep for the chip key before changing it.
- The pipeline view still shows the chip bar for a URL `q` but has no search box, so it shows only the "doesn't apply these filters" note and Clear filters. The task said to remove the search chip everywhere, so I did not add a replacement. A reviewer may want a label there instead.
